heading: Doctrine as a weight vector, and temperature as the mechanism for being baited
body:
Lori, 2026-09-04, after a walk through the Maxis lineage: "Temperature is a good mechanism. As is a vector for actions." BANKED, NOT BUILT. Nothing in Nav.Tactics changes on the strength of this entry.

THE MECHANISM, from The Sims (2000). An agent contains no plan. Each OBJECT advertises what needs it can satisfy and by how much -- a fridge advertises hunger, a bed advertises energy -- and the sim weights each advertisement by how badly it wants that thing right now, then picks. The intelligence lives in the world; the agent holds a max() loop. Wright called it smart terrain. Its practical payoff is that an expansion pack's new object needed no AI change: every existing sim already knew what to do with it.

WHAT LORI TOOK FROM IT, in their words, two things.

  A VECTOR FOR ACTIONS. Doctrines stop being different CODE and become different WEIGHTINGS over the same advertisements. GuardDoctrine and PatrolDoctrine would share one scan and differ by a row in a table. The property that makes this worth having is not elegance, it is that a weight vector can be SWEPT and MEASURED -- see [[measure-before-deciding]] -- where a decision tree can only be read. A pad advertises repair, a chokepoint advertises cover, a wounded squadmate advertises support.

  TEMPERATURE. Richard Evans, AI lead on The Sims 3, chose actions with a Boltzmann distribution over the utilities, with a TEMPERATURE that is low when the sim is happy and HIGH when it is doing badly -- so a desperate agent is measurably more likely to take a low-utility action. Stress makes you erratic, expressed as one number.

WHY TEMPERATURE IS THE INTERESTING ONE HERE, and this is the whole reason it was banked rather than noted and dropped. This project exists for "guards that never retreat to repair and patrols that get baited". A PERFECT UTILITY MAXIMISER CANNOT BE BAITED -- that is what makes it a maximiser. So the exploitable imperfection is not a defect to be tolerated in a doctrine engine, it is the product. The Sims literature says it should be a KNOB rather than an accident of a decision tree's branch ordering, and Maxis broke their own optimiser three separate ways on purpose:
  - The sim does not pick the best. It picks at random from among the TOP SCORERS, because argmax "felt robotic and overly predictable" and a sim that meets its needs perfectly leaves the player nothing to do.
  - Evans' temperature, above.
  - The urinal rule: realistic bathroom spacing was implemented and then CUT, because correct behaviour was dull and random choice produced memorable moments.
A squad whose decision quality degrades under pressure is both plausible and precisely the thing a player learns to induce. That is the closest thing to a mechanism for "baitable" that has turned up.

THE CRITICISM, which is the half that will bite, and it is the same charge as SimLife. Utility systems are ILLEGIBLE as they grow: the structure that makes them extensible is the structure that makes "why did it do that" unanswerable, and behaviour trees' rigid transitions are called out as both their weakness and their strength for exactly this reason. Three more, all reported by practitioners rather than theorised: OSCILLATION between two near-equal scores re-evaluated every tick, whose standard fix is inertia, which is another tuning parameter; BREAKDOWN AT FINE GRANULARITY, where it works for goal selection and falls apart used for every action because there are too many values to hold in your head; and GLOBAL TUNING, because every advertisement competes in one scalar space, so adding a candidate silently re-weights everything already in it.
FOR THIS PROJECT THAT IS AN ARGUMENT FOR THE VIEWER, not against the mechanism. A weighting is exactly the kind of thing the inspector can show -- every candidate, its advertisement, its weighted score, and which one won -- and that is the difference between SimLife and SimAnt, where the pheromone trails were DRAWN and people actually learned something.

RED ALERT IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE, not the model, and I had this wrong first. I described its target selection as an advertisement scan; the actual code is 1996 C++ with a deep per-type class hierarchy, and any scoring is buried in overrides. Lori, having opened it: "Just briefly looking at the code I see it has tons of individual functions just for aircraft... I didn't even get out of the As." The aircraft sprawl is honest rather than sloppy -- aircraft do not pathfind through cells at all, and need landing, ammo and return-to-base, none of which fits the ground abstraction -- but the lesson stands: RA put the STATS in data (rules.ini, which is why the modding scene existed) and left the BEHAVIOUR in a class per unit type. The Sims put the behaviour in the data too. Same era, opposite call, and Lori's data-over-code position is the Sims one. See [[data-over-code]].
A WARNING THAT FOLLOWS FROM IT: MovementSystem is a grid, the same as RA's. If air ever arrives here it will not fit, and it will grow its own everything for the same honest reason.

CLEAN ROOM. The C&C and Red Alert sources are public since 2020/2025 under GPL v3 at github.com/electronicarts/CnC_Red_Alert. Reading is fine; identifiers, constants and transcribed structure must never reach this repo, and with GPL that is a licensing question rather than only hygiene. Nothing in this entry is transcribed -- the RA characterisation above is from general knowledge and from Lori's own glance, and it is recorded here as a NEGATIVE example. See [[clean-room-no-competitor-source]].

SOURCES, all public commentary rather than source: Mark Brown, "The Genius AI Behind The Sims" (gmtk.substack.com); Wikipedia "Utility system" and "Richard Evans (AI researcher)"; Dave Mark's Infinite Axis Utility System (gameai.com/iaus.php), the modern descendant; and practitioner write-ups on oscillation and granularity. Searched 2026-09-04: there is NO commentary on Red Alert's AI specifically -- the source-release coverage is entirely preservation and modding.

NOT DECIDED, and deliberately left open: whether any of this displaces SquadDoctrine's current shape, what a squad's "need" even is, and whether temperature belongs to a squad or to an agent. Lori called the mechanisms good; that is not a build order.
